newsitem.title: USA: Cao Limn loadings delayed by 10-20 days-trade.
newsitem.headline: Cao Limn loadings delayed by 10-20 days-trade.

text.p: Loadings of Cao Limn crude oil in Colombia are being delayed by 10-20 days under new July and August schedules hammered out in the wake of crippling rebel attacks on the Cao Limn-Coveas pipeline, trade sources said on Wednesday.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol has at least three cargoes that were affected by the shutdown.
The company is still negotiating final dates with Petrotrin, Trinidad and Tobago's state oil company, for a 525,000 barrel cargo originally scheduled to load July 26-28.
Ecopetrol had proposed a 20-day delay, but Petrotrin could still receive the cargo sooner pending final agreement, trade sources said.
Spain's Repsol had purchased two Ecopetrol cargoes originally loading in July and August. These are expected to be delayed by about 15 days.
Customers that bought Cao Limn cargoes from equity producers Occidental and Shell are experiencing delays of 10-12 days.

Ecopetrol's schedule is further behind, trade sources said, because the state company has obligations to supply local refineries and may also try to re-fill a two-million barrel floating storage facility offshore Coveas.
Occidental has three affected cargoes totalling 1.405 million barrels. These have been bumped back by about 10 days.
"We're about 10 days behind. By the end of the year, we expect to catch up," an Occidental spokesman said.

Among Oxy's affected clients was Repsol, which buys Latin American crude for its La Pampilla refinery in Peru. Repsol's Oxy cargo, originally scheduled to load July 28-30, has been pushed back to August 8-10.
Shell's affected cargoes, including another one to Repsol, are expected to experience 10-12 day delays, trade sources said.

Among the other end-users impacted by the shutdown is Amoco, which bought two Cao cargoes totalling one million barrels from Coastal and Elf. These companies had purchased the cargoes from Oxy and Shell.
The shipments, originally scheduled to co-load around July 15-17, are now set for around July 27-29.
Ecopetrol declared force majeure on Cao Limn loadings on July 6 and lifted it on July 21.
Although the company often declares force majeure in response to frequent rebel bombings of the pipeline, this shutdown was unusually long after back-to-back attacks.
The attacks forced Occidental to declare force majeure on the 175,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cao Limn field on July 15, the first time the company has had to take this measure in Colombia.
Oxy, which operates the field, lifted force majeure on the field on July 18.
The 250,000-300,000 bpd pipeline has been blown up about 37 times so far this year.
All of the attacks are thought to be the work of National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels, who dynamited the pipeline 47 times last year and spilled more than 105,000 barrels of crude.
((--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620))
